title: Honest Interval Length for High-Dimensional Genomic Mediation Sums with Cancelling Pathways
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS, but sharp original-law frontier and simultaneous adaptation remain undelivered; normalized incremental tier and paper-score ceiling 4.5 fall below field floor 7.4, independently confirmed as no bounded repair.
gap_reasons: The promised field-level contribution—a sharp, original-law two-scale honest-length profile with a bounded-dimensional evaluable decision game and matched upper/lower frontier—is not a theorem in this core: it remains explicitly open, while the delivered null/regular lower comparisons, loose upper rule, and growing finite-n LP certificates are a strictly weaker kernel.

The advertised simultaneous adaptation factor is only posed as an unresolved question; finite-n approximation of its value does not supply the requested limiting value, evaluable limiting game, or sharp common-rule frontier needed for the claimed contribution.

The lower-bound theorem is framed as a partial benchmark, but the note does not establish theorem-level novelty for that standalone result versus the credited Cai--Guo lower-bound architecture; it cannot carry the claimed sharp-frontier positioning by itself.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 established an original-law null lower benchmark, a certified regular-scale lower comparison, a loose exact-honest data-only upper construction, and finite-sample decision programs; D0.5 math passed with zero findings. The sharp original-law profile and limiting simultaneous adaptation factor remain explicit open problems, and the regular-scale upper/lower gap diverges as sqrt(n d_n), so the delivered package was graded incremental below the field floor. Independent validity review found no bounded faithful repair; re-raise only with genuinely new full-class upper-completeness and covariance/support geometry results, never an identical retry.
tldr:
Genomic mediation targets a signed sum whose component pathways can cancel. Under a Gaussian exposure--mediator--outcome system with a sparse outcome regression, dense exposure loading, and unknown mediator covariance, global honesty can impose positive interval length even at the joint null. The focal objects are the sharp normalized length frontier \(L_n(
u)/d_n\) and the simultaneous adaptation factor \(\mathcal A_n(K)\). The frontier retains the weak scale \(
u^2\asymp d_n\), the regular crossover \(
u\asymp\sqrt n\,d_n\), and the intermediate region. The unresolved target is a complete original-law interval decision characterization, including whether exact-honest rules attain the limiting frontier, together with a sharp cross-slice converse. A covariance/support optimization tests the adequacy of scalar hidden-bias geometry before it is used. Sharp constants, weak-scale matching, and the adaptation cost are outputs, not assumptions.
gap: Lin--Guo--Sun--Lin supply same-target loaded-score inference, while Cai--Guo supply unknown-covariance sparse mixtures and honest-length orders. These verified ingredients discard or do not optimize the constants that govern connected intervals when score noise and hidden support uncertainty coexist. A lower subexperiment does not settle the full-model upper comparison.
fill: The kernel derives the original-law decision frontier and its optimal simultaneous adaptation cost. Exact Gaussian likelihoods, sparse-support mixtures, and jointly calibrated loaded scores supply the starting moves. Arbitrary covariance geometry and weak-scale interpolation are tested explicitly. A failure of a scalar or finite-dimensional reduction must yield quantified sharp envelopes.
